column3: Places recitation in a disciplined response, while adding a preparatory practice rather than the target's following command.
Presents the Qur'an as free of crookedness, supporting an intelligible, non-deviant course without reducing following to one sense.
Shows followers unable to transfer the consequences of their allegiance to leaders, developing the responsibility reading.
Makes following a means step by step, supporting both ordered adherence and a route-like secondary reading.
Precedes the target by assigning the gathering and recitation to the same speaker, grounding the recitation whose sequence is followed.
Its pursuit language concerns an absent claimant after punishment; it only remotely echoes responsibility after action.
Repetition of following a means highlights renewed, disciplined use of a given course rather than one-off imitation.
Follows the target with clarification, keeping recitation, following, and explanation distinct but consecutive operations.
Contrasts following divine approval with returning under wrath, preserving a moral-route reading alongside recitation.
The event marker has no clear contribution beyond a formal temporal resemblance.
The surah's movement toward the Lord gives a broader directional context, but not a reading instruction.
Shows consequences attached to those who led others, contributing the secondary accountability dimension of following.
The event marker does not clarify recitation or following.
Locates diverse exemplars within the Qur'an, supporting its coherent communicative scope without specifying how to follow its recitation.
Commands measured recitation, furnishing a close parallel for ordered verbal delivery while remaining a distinct practice.
The surrounding event imagery does not add to the target's command.
Its gathering of bones forms a nearby assembly parallel, while not collapsing bodily gathering into verbal recitation.
Contrasts remaining with those who remember God against following desire, clarifying that following can name rival, value-laden courses.
Names divine teaching of the Qur'an, supporting the source-and-reception setting for the target without defining following.

Following Abraham marks enacted affiliation, a parallel that broadens following beyond vocal repetition.
Describes pursuit by one group of another, offering only a non-instructional sense of following.

Being driven toward punishment is a contrary, coercive procession rather than following a recitation.
Characterizes the Qur'an as Arabic for understanding, supporting intelligibility but only secondarily an ordered course.
An oath by the Qur'an with remembrance does not specify recitation or following.
The nearby restoration of bodily detail sustains the surah's assembly motif without supplying a verbal-following parallel.
The Qur'an's majesty alone offers little clarification of following its recitation.
Links sent-down Qur'an with a structured devotional response, reinforcing recitation as transmitted and practicable instruction.
Looking toward the Lord extends the surah's directional field, but does not establish the target's verbal sequence.
Recited Qur'an met without prostration shows that hearing a recitation can call for response, though not specifically following it.
Refusal to alter what is revealed strongly supports fidelity to received wording and sequence, not autonomous revision.
Its tightly joined crisis image only faintly echoes sequence and following.
Moses' request to follow for instruction presents following as patient, ordered learning rather than immediate possession of knowledge.
The later being made to follow the earlier supplies a sequence parallel, including a possible consequence reading rather than recitation itself.
The divine source named before teaching the Qur'an supports the speaker's authority, but adds no direct instruction.
Complete recitation not producing belief distinguishes faithful delivery from the hearer's response; following is not automatic.
The command after completion does not clearly illuminate the target.
The prohibition on hastening with the tongue directly frames the target as reception after divine recitation, not anticipatory self-recitation.
Calling it a noble Qur'an gives status but little guidance on following its recitation.
Pursuit of a snatcher is a punitive chase, only a distant non-verbal analogue.
The surrounding fearful expectation does not clarify the target.
Presents the Qur'an as a coherent, exalted whole, supporting its recitation as more than detached fragments.
Commands attentive listening and silence when the Qur'an is recited, closely defining a receptive posture alongside following.
Love of the immediate supplies a direct contrary to the prior restraint from haste and patient reception of recitation.
Makes following contingent on apparent victory, a contrasting model of allegiance rather than fidelity to revealed recitation.
The summons has no clear relation to recitation or following.
Human creation alone does not clarify the target.
Readers of earlier scripture provide a comparative continuity check, while not becoming the source of the received recitation.

Sets a test for claimed guidance: produce a more guiding book that can be followed, preserving the route dimension.
A repeated command to read highlights recitation as an active commanded act, without specifying its ordered following.
The death-threshold context continues the surah's measured progression but does not gloss the target.
Followers' failed appeal to leaders strengthens the accountability reading while remaining distinct from recitation.
Describes the Qur'an as wise, supporting an ordered and directive discourse without selecting a single reading of following.
The recognition of separation contributes the surah's later transition, not a direct interpretation of recitation.
A second event following the first supports ordered succession, with a secondary consequence reading rather than verbal imitation.
Remembrance at will does not directly clarify following a recitation.
The opening oath establishes the resurrection frame that surrounds the target, but offers no direct lexical parallel.
What follows charity is harm in a different construction; it only weakly shows that succession can alter an act's result.
The counter-summons has no clear value for the target.
The bleak faces belong to nearby judgment imagery and do not explain recitation.
Names believers who follow the messenger, supporting communal, enacted following while not identifying it with reciting.
Voluntary remembrance does not materially clarify the command.
A soul arriving with driver and witness gives a coercive procession, not the target's receptive following.
Questions failure to follow an order, showing that following may involve contested purposes and cannot be reduced to mechanical literalism.

The embryonic reference only participates in a broad nearby bridge of measured formation.
Pursuit in the night-flight narrative offers both planned movement and hostile tracking, a secondary contrast to the target.
The oath image does not illuminate recitation or following.
The bright faces provide only broad surah context.
Following a gift with harm is a different relational sequence, only distantly relevant to consequences of what follows.

The sign introduced by an event marker does not clarify the target.
The night is described as firmer in speech, offering a recitational discipline parallel without directly defining following.
Reading one's own record links reading to personal accountability, a secondary extension rather than the target's immediate scene.
Describes making the Qur'an into fragments, a useful contrary to receiving its recitation as an integrated whole.
A reminder and a path to the Lord reinforce the directional reading, while leaving it secondary to recitation.
A third repetition of following a means confirms sustained method across changing settings, not mere vocal echo.
The second sign has no clear relevance to the target.
The oath's extraction image does not materially clarify recitation or following.
Opposes obedience to Noah with following a ruinous leader, preserving rival guidance and accumulating responsibility as real possibilities.
Pairs the Book with a clear Qur'an, supporting the textual identity of what is recited but not its required following.
Calls the Qur'an guidance and criterion in a ritual setting, only indirectly supporting a route-like reading.
Names the sent-down Arabic Qur'an for understanding, supporting intelligible reception but not the sequence instruction itself.
The death and burial sequence does not clarify the target.
Combines listening with following the best of speech, directly supporting responsive discernment rather than passive hearing alone.

Following desire is a strong contrary: abandoning given signs does not leave neutrality but substitutes another guide.
Links the misleader and those who follow it to a shared outcome, developing the consequence and responsibility reading.
Directly commands following what is revealed, closely supporting the target as practical adherence to received revelation.
Names the sent-down Book and explicitly commands following it, the closest omitted parallel to practical adherence to recited revelation.
Commands following what has been sent down from the Lord and contrasts it with other protectors, preserving rival-guidance possibilities.
Commands following what is revealed and patience until judgment, joining revelation-bound adherence to the anti-haste context.
Describes a Qur'an differentiated for recitation to people at measured intervals, directly supporting paced, ordered delivery.
Forbids hastening with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed, a direct parallel to 75:16-18's restrained reception.
States that the Qur'an was arranged in measured recitation, directly supporting sequence and ordered delivery without reducing following to one sense.
Commands recitation of the Qur'an and connects guidance to the recipient, closely pairing recitation with an ensuing response.
Commands reciting what has been revealed of the Book, directly paralleling reception and enacted use of revealed speech.
Commands following the best of what has been sent down before punishment, a direct adherence parallel that retains an evaluative response.
Commands holding firmly to what is revealed, reinforcing steadfast adherence to the received discourse.
Shows listeners attending to the Qur'an, then returning to warn their people, giving a reception-to-transmission sequence.
Calls for reflection on the Qur'an, supplying a non-mechanical mode of receiving recited discourse.
Reports hearing a wondrous Qur'an that guides to rightness and elicits belief, a close reception-and-response parallel.
Commands reciting what is feasible of the Qur'an, complementing 73:4's measured-recitation discipline.
The opening command to read in the Lord's name gives a foundational recitation command, though its scene differs from 75:18.
Describes those who recite the Book with its due recitation and believe it, linking recitation with faithful reception.
Names the messenger's recitation of divine signs and ensuing formation, supporting recitation as formative communication.
Identifies those who follow the messenger associated with recited revelation, joining messenger-following and revealed speech.
The one who sheds the signs and is followed by Satan supplies a strong contrary: departing revelation opens a rival following.
Commands recitation of what has been revealed from the Book and denies alteration of its words, reinforcing source-bound fidelity.
When divine signs are recited, the prophets' heirs fall in prostration and weeping, showing embodied response without making it automatic.
The complaint that the Qur'an was taken as abandoned gives a direct contrary to following its recitation.
The command not to listen to the Qur'an and to disrupt it is a direct contrary to attentive reception.
Describes the messenger reciting signs, purifying, and teaching the Book, supporting recitation as ordered instruction.
Describes a messenger reciting clear signs to bring believers from darkness to light, tying recitation to directed transition.
Names a messenger who recites purified pages, supporting a transmitter-and-received-text setting.
Prays for a messenger who recites signs and teaches the Book, giving an earlier formulation of recitation as instruction.
Again joins recitation of signs with purification and teaching, supporting the communicative function of recitation.
Following inherited practice despite lacking guidance supplies a contrary model of unexamined following.
Requires return to God and the messenger in dispute, supporting accountable adherence while not naming recitation.
Warns against following a path other than the believers after guidance becomes clear, adding a consequence-oriented route reading.
Commands judgment by revealed scripture and warns against desires, preserving revelation versus desire as competing guidance.
Commands judging by what God has sent down and not following desires, a close rival-guidance contrast.
Limits the messenger to following what is revealed, supporting obedience to a received source rather than self-direction.
Commands following what has been revealed from the Lord, a direct revealed-guidance parallel outside the recitation wording.
Commands following the straight path and not divergent paths, strengthening the route reading without selecting it over recitation.
Warns against following desires after knowledge has come, preserving the contrast between received knowledge and rival courses.
Assigns clarification of what was sent down, complementing 75:19's later explanation after recitation.
Reports hearers falling in prostration when the Qur'an is recited, a receptive-response parallel to 84:21.
Promises that whoever follows divine guidance will neither go astray nor suffer, extending the guidance-path reading.
Shows hostile reaction when clear signs are recited, confirming that recitation can meet resistant rather than receptive hearing.
Addresses those whose signs had been recited to them but who turned away, a contrary reception pattern.
Recalls signs recited to hearers who denied them, distinguishing delivery from acceptance.
Asks whether the Book recited to them is sufficient, directly foregrounding an ongoing recitation before its audience.
Commands remembrance of what is recited in the households, coupling recited signs with recollection.
Describes people who recite God's Book and sustain worship and giving, a communal enacted-reading parallel.
Presents the Book as a coherent, reiterated discourse that moves hearers bodily, supporting integrated reception of Qur'anic speech.
Describes a Book whose signs are detailed as an Arabic Qur'an for knowing people, supporting intelligible structured discourse.
Depicts one who hears divine signs recited yet persists arrogantly, a contrary to responsive following.
Shows clear signs recited and rejected as magic, another contrary reception that keeps delivery distinct from assent.
States that the Qur'an was made easy for remembrance, supporting accessibility while not itself defining following.
